newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ASC raises concern on profit forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ASC raises concern on profit forecasts.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Wednesday that companies should perhaps be barred from projecting earnings when marketing shares to the public.
The corporate watchdog's chairman, Alan Cameron, expressed concern that well under half of the earnings forecasts included in prospectuses for Australian share issues were never met.
He distinguished between forecasts, which were based on the most probable economic outlook, and projections, which were not.

"There may be a case to say that projections as such ought not to be allowed, having regard to the definition I was just suggesting," Cameron told a luncheon hosted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Australia in Melbourne.
Most investors recognise the unreliability of even cautious profit forecasts, but gullible investors may not, he said.
"I think that investors like to see them but I think investors also know they should be taken with a grain of salt," Cameron said.
